insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: ₹2 lakhs / ₹3 lakhs / ₹4 lakhs / ₹5 lakhs / ₹7 lakhs / ₹10 lakhs

great.name: No Claim Bonus
great.quote: An Additional Sum Insured of 10% of Annual Sum Insured provided on each renewal for every claim-free year up to a maximum of 50%. In case of a claim under the policy, the accumulated Additional Sum Insured will be reduced by 10% of the Annual Sum Insured in the following year.
great.reference: Key Information Sheet: Renewal Benefits (a) / Policy Wordings Part II, Section 2 (G) Additional Sum Insured (Cumulative Bonus)
great.explanation: Additional Sum Insured increases by 10% each claim-free renewal year up to 50%. After a claim, it reduces by 10% (not to zero), so you retain most of the built-up bonus.

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: Co-payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/insured/proposer will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
great.explanation: Only a glossary definition of co-payment is provided and no applied co-pay clause is stated here. That typically means no co-pay is charged and the insurer pays 100% of admissible claims (unlike many plans that add 10–20% co-pay).

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months (48 months for plans with Sum Insured up to 2Lacs) of continuous coverage
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Clause 3.1 (Code-Excl01) / Key Information Sheet: Waiting Period (a)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for 24 months, and for Sum Insured up to ₹2 lakhs the waiting period is 48 months. Claims for declared/known conditions will be payable only after this waiting period is completed.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Clause 3.2 (Code-Excl02) / Key Information Sheet: Waiting Period (b)
good.explanation: Listed diseases/surgeries are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. This delays payouts for certain common planned procedures in the initial years.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Clause 3.4 (Code-Excl03) / Key Information Sheet: Waiting Period (d)
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days from policy start, while accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard clause that can block early non-accident claims.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: For plans with Sum Insured ` 3lacs and above, We will reset up to 100% of the Sum insured once in a policy year... The reset amount can only be used for all future claims within the same policy year, not related to the illness/ disease/ injury for which a claim has been paid in that policy year for the same person
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Section 2 (Scope of Cover), (E) Reset Benefit / Key Information Sheet: Reset Benefit
good.explanation: For Sum Insured ₹3 lakhs and above, up to 100% of Sum Insured is restored once per policy year. The restored amount can be used only for a different illness/injury than the one already claimed for by the same person in that year.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-hospitalisation Medical Expenses incurred by You for a 30-day period immediately prior to Your Hospitalisation
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Section 2 (C) Pre-Hospitalisation and Post-Hospitalisation Expenses / Key Information Sheet: Pre & Post Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps pay for consultations and tests leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post-hospitalisation Medical Expenses incurred by You for a 60-day period immediately post Hospitalisation
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Section 2 (C) Pre-Hospitalisation and Post-Hospitalisation Expenses / Key Information Sheet: Pre & Post Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge are covered. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Below are the non payable items applicable in the policy... List of Non Payable Items as per IRDAI... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 57 NEBULISATION KIT ... 58 RECOVERY KIT, ETC]ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED
bad.reference: Policy Wordings: Non Payables (List of Non Payable Items as per IRDAI)
bad.explanation: Consumables and many routine hospital items (e.g., gloves, masks, kits) are listed as non-payable. You may have to pay these out of pocket even during an otherwise covered hospitalization.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: (a) Cataract, where sub-limit of ` 20,000/- is applicable per eye per Policy year for Plans with Sum Insured up to 5 Lacs... (b) Sub limit options of A and B available for Sum Insured option 2 lacs and Sub limit C option is available for 3 lacs/ 4 lacs/ 5 lacs
bad.reference: Key Information Sheet: Sub Limit (a), (b) / Policy Wordings Clause 3.2 and Extension 15 (Sub Limits)
bad.explanation: Rupee sub-limits apply for certain treatments such as cataract at ₹20,000 per eye per policy year (for Sum Insured up to ₹5 lakhs). If your hospital bill exceeds the sub-limit, the extra amount will be payable by you.

bad.name: Cashless Network
bad.quote: Cashless Facility available at over 4000+ network hospitals.
bad.reference: Key Information Sheet: Payout Basis / Claim Administration
bad.explanation: Cashless treatment is available at 4,000+ network hospitals. This is below the common 7,000+ benchmark, so you may have fewer cashless options in some cities.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.reference: Key Information Sheet: Clause 2. Scope of the Cover (Reset Benefit)
bad.explanation: Reset benefit is not available for at least one plan variant as shown in the Key Information Sheet. Without restore, your Sum Insured may get exhausted after a large claim in the same policy year.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: Room Rent means the amount charged by a hospital for the occupancy of a bed on per day (24 hours) basis and shall include associated medical expenses.
unclear.reference: Policy Wordings Part II: Definitions (Room Rent)
unclear.explanation: Only the definition of room rent is provided here and no eligible room category or cap is stated in this extract. The actual room eligibility (and whether proportionate deductions can apply) would need to be confirmed from the plan schedule/benefit table.
